rows.subtopic: Probability from a Collection of Objects
rows.stem: A bag contains 3 red balls, 5 white balls and 7 black balls. The probability that a ball drawn from the bag at random will be neither red nor black is :
rows.solution:
The bag holds \(3 + 5 + 7 = 15\) balls. A ball that is neither red nor black is white, and there are 5 white balls.

\(P(\text{neither red nor black}) = \dfrac{5}{15} = \dfrac{1}{3}\), which is option (A) \(\dfrac{1}{3}\).

rows.stem: The probability of getting a bad egg in a lot of 400 eggs is 0.045. The number of good eggs in the lot is :
rows.solution:
Number of bad eggs \(= 0.045 \times 400 = 18\).

Number of good eggs \(= 400 - 18 = 382\). (Equally, \(P(\text{good egg}) = 1 - 0.045 = 0.955\), and \(0.955 \times 400 = 382\).)

This is option (C) \(382\).

rows.stem: The mean of five numbers is 15. If we include one more number, the mean of six numbers becomes 17. The included number is :
rows.solution:
Sum of the five numbers \(= 5 \times 15 = 75\). Sum of the six numbers \(= 6 \times 17 = 102\).

The included number is \(102 - 75 = 27\), which is option (A) \(27\).

rows.subtopic: Zeroes and Coefficients of a Quadratic Polynomial
rows.stem: What should be added from the polynomial \(x^2 - 5x + 4\), so that 3 is the zero of the resulting polynomial ?
rows.solution:
The question's "added from" is a slip for "added to".

Let k be added. Then 3 is a zero of \(x^2 - 5x + 4 + k\):

\(3^2 - 5 \times 3 + 4 + k = 0\), that is \(-2 + k = 0\), so \(k = 2\).

This is option (B) \(2\).

rows.subtopic: Irrational Numbers and Proof by Contradiction
rows.stem: The smallest irrational number by which \(\sqrt{20}\) should be multiplied so as to get a rational number, is :
rows.solution:
\(\sqrt{20} = \sqrt{4 \times 5} = 2\sqrt{5}\), and \(2\sqrt{5} \times \sqrt{5} = 2 \times 5 = 10\), which is rational.

Among the choices, 5 is not irrational, and \(\sqrt{20} \times \sqrt{2} = \sqrt{40} = 2\sqrt{10}\) is irrational. Both \(\sqrt{5}\) and \(\sqrt{20}\) give a rational product (10 and 20), and the smaller of the two is \(\sqrt{5}\).

This is option (D) \(\sqrt{5}\).

rows.subtopic: Number of Tangents from an External Point
rows.stem: From an external point P, two tangents PA and PB are drawn to the circle with centre O. Prove that OP is the perpendicular bisector of chord AB.
rows.solution:
Figure: a circle with centre O and an external point P; the tangents PA and PB touch the circle at A and B, and the chord AB meets OP at C.

In triangles OAP and OBP:

\(OA = OB\) (radii),

\(\angle OAP = \angle OBP = 90^\circ\) (a radius is perpendicular to the tangent at its point of contact),

OP is common.

So \(\Delta OAP \cong \Delta OBP\) (RHS), which gives \(PA = PB\) and \(\angle APO = \angle BPO\) (CPCT).

In triangles ACP and BCP:

\(PA = PB\), \(\angle APC = \angle BPC\), and PC is common.

So \(\Delta ACP \cong \Delta BCP\) (SAS), which gives \(AC = BC\) and \(\angle ACP = \angle BCP\) (CPCT).

A, C and B lie on one line, so \(\angle ACP + \angle BCP = 180^\circ\). The two angles are equal, so each is \(90^\circ\), and \(OP \perp AB\).

OP is perpendicular to AB and passes through its mid-point C, so OP is the perpendicular bisector of the chord AB.

rows.stem: A man on a cliff observes a boat at an angle of depression of \(30^\circ\) which is approaching the shore to the point immediately beneath the observer with a uniform speed. Six minutes later, the angle of depression of the boat is found to be \(60^\circ\). Find the time taken by the boat from here to reach the shore.
rows.solution:
Figure: the observer is at B on top of the cliff AB of height h, with A at the foot on the shore. P is the first position of the boat and Q its position six minutes later, with P, Q and A on one line. Let \(AQ = x\) and \(PQ = y\).

The angle of depression from B equals the angle of elevation of B from the boat (alternate angles), so \(\angle BQA = 60^\circ\) and \(\angle BPA = 30^\circ\).

In triangle QAB, \(\tan 60^\circ = \dfrac{h}{x}\): \(\sqrt{3} = \dfrac{h}{x}\), so \(h = \sqrt{3}x\) ... (i)

In triangle PAB, \(\tan 30^\circ = \dfrac{h}{x + y}\): \(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{h}{x + y}\), so \(x + y = \sqrt{3}h\) ... (ii)

Substituting (i) in (ii): \(x + y = \sqrt{3} \times \sqrt{3}x = 3x\), so \(y = 2x\).

The boat moves at a uniform speed and covers \(y = 2x\) in 6 minutes, so it covers x in \(\dfrac{1}{2} \times 6 = 3\) minutes.

The boat takes 3 minutes from Q to reach the shore.
